To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a nonparametric test for comparing two networks based on the geometry of the graph Laplacian, and (2) we show that this test is more statistically powerful than a mass-univarite approach, and (3) we have also proposed a method for visualizating the individual contribution of an edge to the overall network test.
The proposed test is more powerful than the mass-univariate test.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of modern geometric and statistical methods for the analysis of functional neuroimaging networks.
the application of statistical methodology to the analysis of network data.
the problem of statistical inference for graph Laplacian networks, and the development of novel methods for hypothesis testing in such settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is an effective and powerful approach for hypothesis testing on network data.
our approach is more statistical powerful than the mass-univariate approach, and provides a more comprehensive visualization of the data than the mass-unvariate approach.
the test statistic proposed in this work is an effective tool to detect differences between two populations in the context of network analysis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have provided a novel methodology for testing hypotheses about the networks, and have illustrated the utility of this approach in the context of functional neuroimaging.
we have provided a novel approach to testing hypotheses on network data.
we have provided a framework for testing hypotheses on network data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of networks as a summary of relational data in neuroimaging can lead to more powerful statistical inferences, and that the geometric structure of networks provides a useful conceptual framework for their statistical analysis.

, in order to test hypotheses on networks, it is essential to consider the geometric properties of the space of network matrices, and to use nonparametric methods for inference on the space of probability measures on this space.
, in the context of network analysis, the use of a single global test statistic is a more appropriate approach than a mass-unvariate one.
